scenarios.name: count-accounts
scenarios.why: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ACCOUNT WHERE ACCOUNT_SORTCODE = '987654' (the program's own sort code): SQLCODE 0 -- 'Y' and NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS 13 (the seed's 987654 rows; the 123456 one is not counted)

scenarios.name: caller-data-initialised
scenarios.why: a COMMAREA full of the caller's values: INITIALIZE DFHCOMMAREA blanks / zeroes the named items (not the FILLERs), then the count and 'Y'

scenarios.name: select-fails
scenarios.why: the SELECT fails -913: 'N', NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS left at the INITIALIZE's zero (FAIL-CODE not set)

notes: CBSA's account-control service (ACCTCTRL; no program in the corpus LINKs it -- the transaction OCAC is the create-account one, which the program never reads -- so the COMMAREA is its own DFHCOMMAREA, the ACCTCTRL copybook's ACCOUNT-CONTROL-RECORD). It INITIALIZEs the COMMAREA and counts the ACCOUNT rows of the program's own sort code (987654) with SELECT COUNT(*) INTO from Db2 (unqualified: the bind's QUALIFIER, IBMUSER); SQLCODE 0 gives 'Y' and the count in NUMBER-OF-ACCOUNTS, any other 'N'. POPULATE-TIME-DATE is never PERFORMed (dead code). The table is compared after every scenario. Data: seed.sql is cbsa-creacc's (SYNTHETIC; CONTROL rows left out: only ACCOUNT is created).
